title: Audit-first deterministic reference kernel
novelty_claim: The research contribution is not another orbit demo, but a tiny Newtonian gravity reference kernel whose core claim is falsifiable auditability: invariant tracking, timestep-convergence checks, and reproducibility across constrained runtimes.
closest_prior_art: REBOUND: An open-source multi-purpose N-body code for collisional dynamics (2011)
Orbital Mechanics Two-Body Model for Educational Purposes (2024)
differentiation: Restrict scope to a minimal direct-sum 2-body/3-body/small-N core rather than claiming a new fast or general N-body engine.
Make conservation diagnostics, analytic controls, and a compact benchmark pack first-class outputs instead of optional validation.
Treat deterministic behavior across browser, WASM, and other low-precision targets as part of the research claim, not a packaging detail.
easiest_falsifier: Novelty fails if an existing lightweight simulator already combines the same audit surface and runtime reproducibility guarantees, or if the kernel cannot meet stated tolerance targets on analytic controls and a trusted baseline comparison.
evidence_plan: Recover circular and elliptical two-body motion, period, escape velocity, and orbital elements against closed-form expectations.
Track total energy, angular momentum, and center-of-mass drift over long horizons.
Run timestep-halving convergence checks until state error and invariant drift stabilize.
Compare matched scenarios against REBOUND or an equivalent trusted direct-sum baseline.
Execute the same scenario bundle in at least two runtimes and record tolerance-bounded reproducibility or failure.

title: Honest close-encounter minimal core
novelty_claim: The under-served gap is a minimal gravity simulator that exposes its safe operating regime during near-collision events through explicit policy choices, sensitivity disclosure, and honest failure reporting.
closest_prior_art: student and hobby gravity simulators with Euler, Verlet, or Barnes-Hut variants
differentiation: Center the contribution on close-encounter robustness rather than large-N speed or another generic sandbox UI.
Make adaptive-step triggers, softening sensitivity, and merge-or-abort rules explicit and benchmarked.
Treat failure envelopes as publishable outputs so the simulator states when it stops being trustworthy.
easiest_falsifier: The claim collapses if a plain fixed-step baseline already survives the chosen close-encounter cases with comparable results, or if mature codes expose the same policies in equally lightweight form.
evidence_plan: Stress unequal masses, high eccentricity, slingshot, and near-collision trajectories.
Ablate no-softening, softening, merge, bounce, and abort policies on identical scenarios.
Measure epsilon and dt sensitivity under the same initial conditions.
Compare trajectories and invariant drift against a trusted baseline in the same regimes.

title: Unit-safe scenario compiler for minimal gravity simulation
novelty_claim: A hidden failure mode in minimal gravity simulators is incoherent mass-distance-time scaling; a unit-safe authoring layer could make small simulators scientifically legible instead of merely visually plausible.
closest_prior_art: educational toy simulators using arbitrary gravitational constants
differentiation: Shift the contribution from propagation breadth to scenario validity and scale safety.
Support dimensionless normalization plus SI-to-normalized conversion for both classroom and real-data scenarios.
Reject or warn on incoherent unit triples before simulation instead of silently producing attractive but meaningless trajectories.
easiest_falsifier: This direction weakens fast if lightweight tools already provide the same normalization guard rails with similar simplicity, or if corrected units do not materially change benchmark outcomes.
evidence_plan: Detect inconsistent units and unstable scale choices before execution.
Round-trip SI-to-normalized-to-SI conversions and verify orbital parameter recovery within tolerance.
Run paired normalized and physical-unit scenarios and confirm matching trajectories.
Curate representative toy scenarios that otherwise fail silently because of unit incoherence.
